competences: The learner read affirmative and negative future sentences.
The learner order words to form grammatical future sentences.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads, spells and uses correctly: will, shall, shall not, will not, future.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to read affirmative and negative future sentences.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to order words to form grammatical future sentences.
priorKnowledge: Learners have read future-time words and familiar present-tense action words.
materials: Word cards for the two sourced jumbled sentences
references: P 4 ENG & SST Lesson Notes Term III 2023
P 4 Composition AND Comprehension Scheme Term III

steps.content: Learners have read future-time words and familiar present-tense action words. Key words: will, shall, shall not, will not, future
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays source subject-verb-action sentence table and links the chart to the prior knowledge: Learners have read future-time words and familiar present-tense action words. The teacher pronounces the lesson vocabulary, checks learners’ reading, and introduces using will and shall.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall familiar words, read the displayed key words aloud, and explain what they already know about the topic.

source.quote: Look at the table below and write five sentences

steps.content: Will and shall: I / We: shall; shall not. She / They: will; will not. play with my friends. go with him. go on holiday. swim in the lake. disturb you today.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: I / We: shall; shall not. She / They: will; will not. play with my friends. go with him. go on holiday. swim in the lake. disturb you today. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Use the sentence table to write five sentences." Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

source.quote: Look at the table below and write five sentences

steps.content: Example 1: We shall not play with him. We shall go with him.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: We shall not play with him. We shall go with him. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Rearrange: tomorrow here my father will come." Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

steps.content: Example 2: Jane will go to school tomorrow. We shall not go to the market next week. We shall not see elephants because they are not in the zoo.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher models reading of this content: Jane will go to school tomorrow. We shall not go to the market next week. We shall not see elephants because they are not in the zoo. The teacher checks pronunciation and meaning, draws attention to the target wording, and asks: "Rearrange: go to India I shall next week." Learners’ responses are checked against the displayed text.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source sentences or entries aloud, identify the target words, answer the teacher’s question, and copy the stated content accurately.

source.quote: Jane will go to school tomorrow

steps.content: Use the sentence table to write five sentences. Rearrange: tomorrow here my father will come. Rearrange: go to India I shall next week.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the following sourced text-based exercise: Use the sentence table to write five sentences. Rearrange: tomorrow here my father will come. Rearrange: go to India I shall next week. The teacher checks learners’ written answers for meaning, spelling and punctuation, using this key: Accept five grammatical combinations of a source subject, will/shall form, and action phrase. Source models: We shall not play with him. We shall go with him. My father will come here tomorrow. I shall go to India next week.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer individually in their books, use full sentences when required, read selected answers aloud, and correct spelling or punctuation after feedback.

source.quote: Look at the table below and write five sentences

steps.content: Key answers: Accept five grammatical combinations of a source subject, will/shall form, and action phrase. Source models: We shall not play with him. We shall go with him. My father will come here tomorrow. I shall go to India next week.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher revisits these questions: Use the sentence table to write five sentences. Rearrange: tomorrow here my father will come. Rearrange: go to India I shall next week. The teacher checks whether learners have met the objectives, explains any remaining errors using the source text, and assigns the final exercise item for correction.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners explain their answers with evidence from the text, read corrected sentences aloud, and note the final item for homework.

source.quote: go to India I shall next week

assessment: Check oral reading and written responses to these questions: Use the sentence table to write five sentences. Rearrange: tomorrow here my father will come. Rearrange: go to India I shall next week. Mark meaning, spelling, sentence structure and punctuation against the displayed source models.
homework: Complete or correct the following source exercise item, writing the answer neatly: Rearrange: go to India I shall next week.
